issues.description: The problem text inconsistently uses two different method names for the animal feeding sound: the UML and several tasks require an abstract method messageOnFeed():String (and the solution/template use messageOnFeed()), but other places in the problem description (the per-animal instructions and Farm feedAllAnimals description) refer to getFeedingSound(). This name mismatch is structural: students may look for or implement getFeedingSound() while the provided/expected code uses messageOnFeed(), causing confusion or failing tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) change all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement to messageOnFeed(), or (B) rename the abstract method and all implementations to getFeedingSound() in template and solution. Prefer option (A) to align the textual instructions with the UML and existing code (messageOnFeed()). Update all task descriptions and the Farm description accordingly.

issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) refers to a feeding-sound accessor named getFeedingSound(), while the UML and the provided/solution code use messageOnFeed() as the abstract method and implementations. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (the method that returns the animal's feeding sound) can confuse students who read the textual instructions and then look for getFeedingSound() in the template code or when implementing classes.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the name for the feeding-sound method consistent across all artifacts. Update the problem statement text (Part 2) to refer to messageOnFeed() (the method declared in the UML and implemented in the solution) instead of getFeedingSound(). Alternatively, if you prefer the name getFeedingSound(), change the UML and all code references to getFeedingSound() so the textual description and code match.
